name: Testing & Debugging
description: Writing automated tests and systematically locating and fixing defects in code.

questions.question: What does a unit test primarily check?
options: That the whole system works end to end in production
That a small, isolated piece of code such as a single function behaves as expected
That the code is formatted correctly
That the application handles heavy load
questions.explanation: Unit tests target the smallest testable units in isolation; end-to-end and load tests are different levels.

questions.question: In pytest, how do you check that result equals expected?
questions.explanation: pytest uses plain assert statements and rewrites them to show detailed failure messages.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a mock in a unit test?
options: To make tests run in parallel
To replace a real dependency (such as a network call) with a controllable stand-in so the test is isolated and deterministic
questions.explanation: Mocks isolate the code under test from slow or unpredictable collaborators and let you assert how they were called.

questions.question: A test sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Flaky tests are non-deterministic, often due to timing, ordering, shared state or external services.

questions.question: Module app.py does 'from requests import get'. A test uses unittest.mock.patch('requests.get') but app still makes real calls. Why?
options: patch only works on classes, not functions
The mock must be created before Python starts
patch replaces the name where it is looked up; app holds its own reference, so you must patch 'app.get'
questions.explanation: The 'where to patch' rule: patch the name in the namespace that uses it, here app.get.

questions.question: Which pytest command runs only tests whose names contain the substring 'login'?
questions.explanation: -k selects tests by keyword expression on names; -m selects by marker and -x stops at the first failure.

practical.title: Test a divide function
practical.instructions: A function divide(a, b) returns a / b and raises ZeroDivisionError when b is 0. Write two pytest test functions: one checking a normal result and one checking that dividing by zero raises ZeroDivisionError.
practical.expected_output: def test_divide(): assert divide(10, 2) == 5 and def test_divide_by_zero(): with pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError): divide(1, 0).

rubric.hint: pytest only collects functions whose names start with test_.
Call divide(1, 0) inside the raises block.

tasks.title: Get started with pytest
tasks.description: Install pytest and follow the Get Started guide. Write your first tests, run them, and read the failure output of a deliberately broken test.
tasks.completion_criteria: A test file with at least 3 passing tests run via the pytest command.

tasks.title: Debug with pdb and breakpoints
tasks.description: Take a buggy script (or introduce an off-by-one bug yourself) and use breakpoint(), step, next and print variables in pdb to find it. Write down the steps you followed.
tasks.completion_criteria: Bug fixed and a short written log of the debugging steps.

tasks.title: Use fixtures, parametrize and mocks
tasks.description: Write tests for a function that calls an external API, using unittest.mock to fake responses. Use pytest fixtures and parametrize to cover edge cases.
tasks.completion_criteria: Tests run offline, cover success and error responses, and use at least one fixture and one parametrized test.

tasks.title: Add a test suite and CI to a project
tasks.description: Add a meaningful test suite to one of your existing projects, measure coverage and raise it above 80%. Configure continuous integration to run tests on every push.
tasks.completion_criteria: CI pipeline green with coverage report above 80%.
